The user wants me to reload the current page. I should use the `click` tool with `text` set to "Reload page" or similar, but looking at the available tools, there isn't a direct "reload" tool.

Actually, looking more carefully at the available tools, I don't see a `click` tool with `text` parameter that can reload a page. The `click` tool requires either `text`, `textMatch`, `selector`, `index`, `x`, `y`, `coordinate_space`, or `expected_name`.

Wait, I need to look at the available tools again. The `click` tool has these parameters:
- `text` (required)
- `textMatch` (optional)
- `selector` (optional)
- `index` (optional)
- `x` (optional)
- `y` (optional)
- `coordinate_space` (required when x/y are used)
- `capture_id` (required when coordinate_space is screenshot)
- `expected_name` (optional)
- `expected_role` (optional)
- `alsoWindow` (optional)

So I could use `click` with `text="Reload page"` or `text="Reload"` to reload the page. But the tool description says "Click an element by ref_id: click({ref_id})" and "Click text: click({text})".

Actually, looking at the tool list more carefully, there is a `click` tool that can click by text. The description says "Click text: click({text})" and "Click by visible text: click({text})".

So I can use `click(text="Reload page")` or `click(text="Reload")` to reload the page.

However, I should also consider that the user might want me to use the `navigate` tool to reload the page, but `navigate` is for changing the URL, not reloading the current page.

Actually, looking at the `navigate` tool description: "Navigate the current tab to a URL and verify that the browser commits the navigation, including same-URL reloads."

So `navigate` could be used with the same URL to reload the page. But `navigate` is typically used to change pages, not reload the current one.

The `click` tool with `text="Reload"` or `text="Reload page"` seems more appropriate for reloading the current page.
